newsitem.title: FRANCE: Basque guerrilla leaders to go on trial in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Basque guerrilla leaders to go on trial in Paris.

text.p: Three leaders of the guerrilla group ETA are among some 40 Basque separatist activists who will go on trial here on Tuesday.
The defendants face up to 10 years in prison on terrorism charges.
If convicted, the three leaders who were detained in the French Basque region five years ago, will serve their sentences in France before being extradited to Spain.
One of them, Francisco "Pakito" Mugica Garmendia, 43, was among the most wanted men in Spain, where he is accused of sending a booby-trapped car to Madrid in 1991.

Spanish police regarded him as the operational chief of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), a group which has killed some 800 people in Spain in a three-decade-long campaign for a separate Basque state.

Also on trial will be Jose Luis "Txelis" Alvarez Santa Cristina, 42, believed to have been ETA's ideologist and financier, in charge of extorting "revolutionary taxes" from businessmen in the Spanish Basque country.
The third defendant, 50-year-old Jose Maria "Fiti" Arregui Erostarbe, is said to be the group's expert on explosives and forged identity documents.
He is wanted in Spain in connection with a parcel bomb which badly maimed Fernando de Mateo Lage, the presiding judge of the Audiencia Nacional anti-terrorist court, in 1990.
All three were captured in a villa in the French Basque resort of Bidart by police investigating ETA's "French commando", a group blamed in Spain for bomb attacks which cost tens of lives.
The group was broken up as it prepared a bomb attack against a government building in the southern Spanish town of Seville before the 1992 World Fair.
Seven suspected members of the group will go on trial on May 26 in a special Paris anti-terrorist court.
That court will try on May 20 a suspected French Basque guerrilla, Jean-Noel Garispe, in connection with a spate of bomb attacks in France by the group Iparetarak in the early 1990s.
